title: Nature/Cell/Science-Quality Figures with cliomicplot
text: Publishing premier scientific journals—Nature, Cell, Science (CNS)—demands strict visual, typographic, statistical discipline: Exact physical trim sizing: Figures must drawn publisher’s printed column widths (e.g., 89 mm single-column, 120 mm 1.5-column, 183 mm double-column) rather arbitrary 7×5 inch canvas scaled typesetting. Minimalist typography data--ink ratio: -figure titles removed (figure explanations belong legend/caption); panel identifier tags (, b, c, d) sit upper left; font sizes constrained 5–7 pt final print scale. Open axes vs. full-box frames: Top right spines removed Nature Science (theme_cli_nature(), theme_cli_science()), structured spines outward ticks preserved Cell SCI/Elsevier styles (theme_cli_cell(), theme_cli_scifig()). Clinical biological integrity: Clinical figures prioritize effect magnitudes raw p-values (e.g. MCID thresholds), track exact denominators, report landmark milestones, present multi-omics evidence side--side. vignette demonstrates cliomicplot creates publication-ready figures matching exact journal requirements, drawing real proteomics, metabolomics, clinical datasets bundled package.

what: 4. Figure 3 — Longitudinal Trajectory with Clinical Severity Bands (Science Style)
title: Nature/Cell/Science-Quality Figures with cliomicplot
text: Individual patient trajectories contain high biological noise. Plotting group means hides clinical heterogeneity, whereas raw spaghetti plots create illegible hairball. Longitudinal Trajectory Plot (Clinical Archetype 4) resolves overlaying semi-transparent individual paths onto shaded clinical severity bands (Mild, Moderate, Severe), anchored bold group mean ribbon visit sample sizes (n=…n = \dots):
code: set.seed(42) n_patients = 24 visits = c("Baseline", "Week 4", "Week 12", "Week 24") traj_df = expand.grid(Patient = paste0("PT-", sprintf("%02d", 1:n_patients)), Visit = visits)  # Simulate clinical response trajectories baseline_scores = rep(runif(n_patients, 50, 85), each = length(visits)) time_drop = rep(c(0, 12, 28, 42), times = n_patients) noise = rnorm(nrow(traj_df), mean = 0, sd = 6) traj_df$Severity = pmax(2, pmin(95, baseline_scores - time_drop + noise))  cliplot(Severity ~ Visit | Patient, data = traj_df,         type = type_trajectory(           severity_bands  = list(Mild = c(0, 25), Moderate = c(25, 50), Severe = c(50, 100)),           severity_colors = c(Mild = "#D9EEF7", Moderate = "#FDE8D7", Severe = "#FADBD8"),           show_mean = TRUE, show_ci = TRUE, show_n = TRUE         ),         theme = "science",         ylab = "Disease Severity Score (0-100)") +   cli_panel_label("c")

what: Figure 1 - X-linked transcriptome dysregulation across immune cells
title: Recreating a Published Figure: SLE X-Chromosome Dysregulation
text: paper’s Figure 1 shows X-linked transcription disturbed SLE. reproduce four panels: () distribution X/-ratio across 27 immune cell types (SLE vs HC), (b) volcano plots X-linked differential expression representative cells immune lineage, (c) mean-logFC heatmap consistently dysregulated X-linked genes per lineage, (d) Normalized Enrichment Score (NES) heatmap immune-related KEGG pathways ranked X/-ratio correlation. Recreated Figure 1 (SLE X-linked dysregulation). Panel : X/-ratio boxplots. Panel b: volcano small multiples representative cells. Panel c: mean logFC heatmap consistently dysregulated X-linked genes lineage. Panel d: KEGG NES heatmap. Panel grouped boxplot jittered points - one cliplot() call: Panel c aggregates per-cell-type DE results gene x lineage matrix mean logFC genes consistently (>= 80% cell types lineage) - -regulated, draws publication heatmap type_heatmap():
code: pat = load_sle("sle_patients.rda")$sle_patients pat$Cell_Type = factor(pat$Cell_Type,                        levels = c("CD16p_Mono", "CL_Mono", "Int_Mono",                                   "NC_Mono", "LDG", "Neu", "mDC", "pDC", ...)) pat$Condition = factor(pat$Condition, levels = c("SLE", "HC"))  cliplot(X_Ratio ~ Cell_Type | Condition, data = pat,         type = type_boxplot(add_jitter = TRUE, jitter_size = 0.55,                             jitter_alpha = 0.3, width = 0.65),         theme = "nature", palette = "nejm") +   labs(x = NULL, y = "X/A ratio") +   cli_panel_label("a") +   theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, size = 6.5),         legend.position = "top", legend.title = element_blank()) de = load_sle("sle_xlinked_de.rda")$sle_xlinked_de de = de[de$Classification != "Non-significant", ] de$Lineage = lineage_map[as.character(de$Cell_Type)]   # lineage_map in script de$Up = de$Classification == "Up-regulated"  consistent_genes = lapply(unique(lineage_map), function(L) {   sub = de[de$Lineage == L, ]   n   = table(lineage_map)[[L]]   uc  = tapply(sub$Up, sub$Gene, sum)   dc  = tapply(sub$Up == FALSE, sub$Gene, sum)   mu  = tapply(sub$logFC[sub$Up], sub$Gene[sub$Up], mean)   md  = tapply(sub$logFC[!sub$Up], sub$Gene[!sub$Up], mean)   data.frame(Gene = c(names(uc)[uc >= 0.8 * n], names(dc)[dc >= 0.8 * n]),              Lineage = L,              logFC = c(mu[names(uc)[uc >= 0.8 * n]],                        md[names(dc)[dc >= 0.8 * n]]),              stringsAsFactors = FALSE) }) consistent_genes = do.call(rbind, consistent_genes)  mat = reshape2::acast(consistent_genes, Gene ~ Lineage, value.var = "logFC") mat[is.na(mat)] = 0  cliplot(mat, type = type_heatmap(scale = "none", cluster_rows = FALSE,                                  cluster_cols = FALSE, show_rownames = TRUE,                                  show_colnames = TRUE, legend_title = "mean logFC"),         theme = "nature")

title: Themes and Palettes in cliomicplot

text: publication figure often want one two genes highlighted detailed annotation box reporting fold-change, confidence interval, exact p-values. type_volcano works plain geom_label_repel; can layer richer annotation top using ggtext::geom_richtext.
code:
# Build annotation for CEACAM5 highlight <- de_results[rownames(de_results) == "CEACAM5", ] highlight$ci_low <- 1.86 highlight$ci_high <- 3.73 highlight$annot <- paste0( "", highlight$gene, "", "

", "Fold change = ", round(highlight$log2FC, 2), "", " (95% CI: ", highlight$ci_low, ", ", highlight$ci_high, ")", "
", "Unadjusted P-value < 0.0001", "
", "Adjusted P-value = ", format(highlight$padj, digits = 2), "" ) # Base volcano from cliplot, then layer annotation p_base <- cliplot(-log10(padj) ~ log2FC, data = de_results, type = type_volcano( pval_cutoff = 0.05, fc_cutoff = 0.25, label_genes = "significant", max_overlaps = 15, point_alpha = 0.60 ), palette = "nature", theme = "nature", title = "Volcano plot with gene annotation call-out", subtitle = expression(FDR < 0.05 * ", |" * log[2] * "FC| > 0.25")) # Layer highlight + annotation on top of the returned ggplot p_annot <- p_base + ggplot2::geom_point( data = highlight, ggplot2::aes(x = log2FC, y = -log10(padj)), inherit.aes = FALSE, shape = 21, size = 5, stroke = 1.4, fill = "#C95C43", colour = "black" ) + ggtext::geom_richtext( data = highlight, ggplot2::aes(x = log2FC - 1.8, y = -log10(padj) + 1.8, label = annot), inherit.aes = FALSE, hjust = 0, vjust = 0.5, size = 3.5, fill = "#F9E5D5", colour = "black", label.colour = NA, label.padding = grid::unit(c(8, 10, 8, 10), "pt") ) + ggplot2::geom_segment( data = highlight, ggplot2::aes(x = log2FC, y = -log10(padj), xend = log2FC - 0.3, yend = -log10(padj) + 0.55), inherit.aes = FALSE, linewidth = 0.5, colour = "#555555" ) p_annot

text: Minimal Clinically Important Difference (MCID) Dumbbell Plot (type_mcid(), Archetype 1): Distinguish genuine clinical relevance large-cohort nominal significance (P<0.001P < 0.001). Connects observed treatment effect sizes validated instrument MCID thresholds (e.g. DLQI = 4.0, EASI = 6.6), point glyphs scaled sample size (NtreatedN_{\text{treated}}) endpoints ordered effect--MCID ratio. Longitudinal Clinical Trajectories Severity Bands (type_trajectory(), Archetype 4): Visualizes patient-level clinical heterogeneity without spaghetti hairballs. Overlays semi-transparent individual trajectories onto shaded background clinical severity bands (Mild, Moderate, Severe), anchored bold group mean trajectory confidence ribbon (95%95\% CI / SE) visit sample-size annotations (n=…n = \dots). Zero-Dependency Native KM & Cumulative Incidence (type_km(), Archetype 5): Completely removed hard dependency survminer. Driven native ggplot2 + survival engine supporting cumulative incidence ([1−S(t)]×100%[1 - S(t)] \times 100\%), landmark milestone callouts (milestones = c(...)) exact percentages directly curve, aligned numbers--risk tables, median survival crosshairs, log-rank pp-values. Clinical Oncology Swimmer Plot Enhancements (type_swimmer(), Archetype 13): Added ongoing therapy indicator rendering arrowheads ends timeline bars patients remaining therapy database lock. Unified clinical event shape/color contracts added duration annotations. Publication Forest Plot Enhancements (type_forest(), Archetype 9): Added alternating background row shading stripes (stripe = TRUE) eliminate horizontal eye drift across wide canvases, unclipped confidence interval labels, zero-magnitude negative sign suppression (-0.00 rounded 0.00), meta-analysis pooled summary diamonds (diamond = TRUE). SCI Full-Box Theme (theme_cli_scifig(), clitheme("scifig")): New publication theme adhering SCI / Elsevier / IEEE journal visual requirements: 4 visible black spines, outward-facing tick marks, subtle dashed reference grid. Expanded Publisher Presets & Compliance Checks (cli_journal_size(), cli_save()): Expanded 9 verified publisher presets (Nature, Nature Communications, Science, Cell, JAMA, NEJM, Lancet, PLOS, IEEE). Added arithmetic printable height verification, support numeric columns (1, 1.5, 2), submission format guidance (warning raster PNG supplied Nature/Science final manuscripts). Exported Standalone Theme Functions: Exported first-class ggplot2 themes theme_cli_nature(), theme_cli_science(), theme_cli_cell(), theme_cli_nejm(), theme_cli_lancet(), theme_cli_scifig(), theme_cli_bw(), theme_cli_classic(), theme_cli_minimal(), theme_cli_dark(), theme_cli_showcase(), theme_cli_broadsheet().
